findings.title: All in-scope success criteria covered with proper test-with pattern and commit discipline
findings.description: File 1 covers exactly the success criteria for Parts 0, A, and D. Every implementation task (T1, T3, T5, T7, T9, T10, T12) is immediately followed by its verify/test task (T2, T4, T6, T8, T11, T13). Commit markers sit at tested, working points (T2, T4, T6, T8, T11, T13) — not after every task and not only at the end. Parts B/C success criteria are correctly deferred to file 2, confirmed by both the projectState frontmatter and the handoff section. No scope creep: every task traces to a design requirement (F002 relocation → T1–T8; Part A → T9–T11; F003 fail-closed → T12–T13; F005 cf verification → T14). Task sizes are proportionate — the largest (T5, 3/5 effort) is the judge-transport extraction, which is well-scoped with clear substeps and a dedicated verify task. No NFRs are restated in the slice design, so no load test or CI wiring task is required.

findings.title: T14 (cf scanning verification) sequenced after T12 (Part D implementation) despite design requiring it before
findings.description: The slice design's Phase 5 note states the cf `archive/`-scanning verification "must appear as its own checklist task in the breakdown, sequenced before Part D lands." T14 is this task and is correctly its own checklist item, but it is numbered after T12 (Part D's implementation) rather than before. The task file mitigates this with explicit gating language in both T12 ("Do not mark this task done until T14's verification outcome is known") and T14 ("This task gates T12 in practice even though it is numbered after it"). A junior AI executing top-to-bottom would implement T12's filename scheme, run T13's tests, then reach T14 — and if T14 finds recursive scanning, would need to revise T12/T13. The task notes the non-recursive case is expected (matching squadron's own non-recursive glob pattern), so rework is unlikely, but reordering T14 before T12 would eliminate the risk entirely and satisfy the design's stated sequence.
